0.long_answer: The gene in question is the TK2 gene. TK2 (thymidine kinase 2) is located on chromosome 16 and is important for the maintenance of mitochondrial DNA. Mutations in this gene lead to TK2 deficiency, a mitochondrial DNA depletion syndrome that typically presents after a period of normal early development. Affected infants begin to show symptoms—such as general muscle weakness—around the age of 2. As the disease progresses, it results in a myopathic condition for which, currently, no definitive treatment exists.
